cards.title: Cisco ASA/FTD VPN Web Server Buffer Overflow RCE
cards.what: A buffer overflow in the VPN web server of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software allows a remote attacker to run arbitrary code. It can be chained with CVE-2025-20362.
cards.why: Successful exploitation gives attackers code execution on internet-facing firewalls, a critical perimeter device, potentially yielding full control and a foothold into the network.
cards.defend: Follow CISA Emergency Directive 25-03 and Cisco advisories: apply fixed software immediately, review for compromise, and disconnect unpatched devices if fixes are unavailable.
cards.product: Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense

cards.title: Google Chrome V8 Type Confusion
cards.what: A type confusion flaw in Chromium's V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine lets a malicious web page corrupt memory in unexpected ways.
cards.why: Simply visiting a crafted site can lead to memory corruption and code execution in the browser process, a common entry point for drive-by attacks.
cards.defend: Update Chrome/Chromium-based browsers to the patched version and enable automatic updates; restart browsers to apply fixes.

cards.title: DELMIA Apriso Insecure Deserialization RCE
cards.what: Dassault Systèmes DELMIA Apriso (manufacturing operations software) deserializes untrusted data unsafely, allowing crafted input to trigger remote code execution.
cards.why: Attackers can run arbitrary code on manufacturing/MES systems, threatening production integrity and providing access to OT-adjacent networks.
cards.defend: Apply Dassault Systèmes patches, restrict network exposure of Apriso, and monitor for anomalous deserialization or unexpected process execution.

cards.title: Linux Kernel TOCTOU Race Condition
cards.what: A time-of-check to time-of-use race condition in the Linux kernel lets an attacker exploit the timing gap between a security check and the use of a resource.
cards.why: Exploitation can compromise confidentiality, integrity, and availability, potentially enabling local privilege escalation on affected systems.
cards.defend: Apply updated kernel packages from your distribution and reboot; limit local access and monitor for unexpected privilege changes.

cards.title: Android Runtime Use-After-Free Privilege Escalation
cards.what: A use-after-free vulnerability in Android Runtime references freed memory, which can be abused to escape the Chrome sandbox and escalate privileges locally.
cards.why: A malicious app or web content could break out of sandbox isolation and gain elevated privileges on the device.
cards.defend: Install the latest Android security update (September 2025 patch level or later) and only install apps from trusted sources.

cards.title: Sitecore Default Machine Key Deserialization RCE
cards.what: Sitecore XM, XP, XC, and Managed Cloud shipped with default ASP.NET machine keys; if left in place, attackers can forge serialized payloads that are deserialized unsafely to run code.
cards.why: Exposed default keys let unauthenticated attackers achieve remote code execution on Sitecore web servers, risking full site and server compromise.
cards.defend: Rotate ASP.NET machine keys to unique values, apply Sitecore's guidance and patches, and monitor for suspicious ViewState or deserialization activity.

cards.title: Sudo Chroot Local Privilege Escalation
cards.what: A flaw in Sudo's -R (--chroot) option lets it load functionality from a user-controlled root directory, pulling in untrusted configuration during evaluation.
cards.why: A local attacker can gain root command execution even when not permitted in the sudoers file, fully compromising the host.
cards.defend: Update Sudo to a fixed release (1.9.17p1 or later); the chroot feature is being deprecated, so avoid relying on it and audit sudoers for chroot usage.

cards.title: Libraesva ESG Attachment Command Injection
cards.what: Libraesva Email Security Gateway fails to safely handle compressed email attachments, allowing OS command injection when a crafted archive is processed.
cards.why: A malicious email alone can trigger code execution on the gateway that inspects all mail, a high-value chokepoint for attackers.
cards.defend: Apply Libraesva's patched versions promptly; monitor gateway processes and outbound connections for anomalous activity tied to attachment scanning.

cards.title: GoAnywhere MFT License Deserialization RCE
cards.what: Fortra GoAnywhere MFT deserializes untrusted data when an actor supplies a forged license response signature, enabling arbitrary object deserialization and possible command injection.
cards.why: Successful exploitation can lead to remote code execution on a file-transfer server, and it is already associated with ransomware campaigns.
cards.defend: Upgrade to a fixed GoAnywhere version, restrict the admin/license interface from internet exposure, and review logs for unexpected deserialization or admin activity.

cards.title: Cisco IOS/IOS XE SNMP Buffer Overflow
cards.what: A stack-based buffer overflow in the SNMP subsystem of Cisco IOS and IOS XE can be triggered by crafted SNMP requests.
cards.why: A low-privileged attacker can crash the device (DoS via reload) and a high-privileged attacker can execute code as root for full device control.
cards.defend: Apply Cisco's fixed software; restrict SNMP access with ACLs, use SNMPv3 with authentication, and disable unused SNMP OIDs where possible.

cards.title: Adminer Server-Side Request Forgery
cards.what: Adminer, a web-based database management tool, can be induced to make server-side requests to attacker-specified destinations.
cards.why: A remote attacker can reach internal services and retrieve potentially sensitive information such as cloud metadata or internal endpoints.
cards.defend: Upgrade Adminer to 4.7.9 or later, avoid exposing it publicly, and restrict access with authentication and network controls.

cards.title: Cisco ASA/FTD VPN Web Server Missing Authorization
cards.what: The VPN web server in Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD lacks proper authorization checks, allowing access to restricted resources.
cards.why: It can be chained with CVE-2025-20333 to escalate impact, and is under active exploitation against internet-facing firewalls.
cards.defend: Follow CISA Emergency Directive ED 25-03 and Cisco guidance to patch or mitigate immediately; review VPN web server logs for unauthorized access.
cards.product: Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense

cards.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Hard-coded Password
cards.what: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (formerly Firepower Management Center) ships with a hard-coded password tied to a low-privileged account. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use these static credentials to log in.
cards.why: FMC is a central control point for firewall policy; even low-privileged access exposes sensitive configuration and operational data, and can be a foothold for deeper compromise of the security fabric.
cards.defend: Apply Cisco's fixed releases per BOD 26-04 guidance, restrict management-plane access to trusted networks, and review logs for unexpected logins from the affected account. Preserve forensic data per CISA's triage requirements before remediating.

cards.title: GNU Bash Shellshock Command Injection
cards.what: A flaw in how Bash parses specially crafted environment variables lets attacker-controlled data be executed as shell commands. This is one of the 'Shellshock' family of Bash vulnerabilities.
cards.why: Any service that passes untrusted input into environment variables before invoking Bash (e.g. CGI, DHCP clients, SSH forced commands) can be tricked into running arbitrary commands, leading to full system compromise.
cards.defend: Patch Bash to a fixed version across all Linux/Unix systems and appliances. Inventory legacy and embedded devices that still ship vulnerable Bash, and monitor web/CGI logs for anomalous environment-based payloads.

cards.title: Jenkins CLI Java Deserialization RCE
cards.what: Jenkins' remoting-based CLI deserializes attacker-supplied Java objects (via a SignedObject) using a fresh ObjectInputStream, bypassing the blocklist protection. This allows unauthenticated remote code execution.
cards.why: Jenkins servers hold source code, build secrets, and deployment credentials, so RCE on a Jenkins controller can compromise an entire software supply chain.
cards.defend: Upgrade Jenkins to a patched version and disable or firewall the CLI remoting port where not needed. Restrict network access to the Jenkins controller and monitor for unexpected CLI connections or child processes.

cards.title: Juniper ScreenOS Backdoor Authentication Bypass
cards.what: Juniper ScreenOS contained unauthorized code enabling a hard-coded/backdoor authentication path, allowing remote administrative login regardless of the configured password. This was the notorious ScreenOS backdoor.
cards.why: An attacker with admin access to a ScreenOS firewall/VPN can alter rules, intercept traffic, and pivot into the protected network, undermining the entire perimeter.
cards.defend: Apply Juniper's fixed ScreenOS releases immediately and rotate all device credentials. Restrict management access to trusted hosts and audit admin login logs for unexplained authentications.

cards.title: Samsung libimagecodec Out-of-Bounds Write RCE
cards.what: An out-of-bounds write in Samsung's libimagecodec.quram.so image parsing library lets a crafted image trigger memory corruption. This can allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.
cards.why: Because image parsing can be triggered by messaging or media, this can enable zero-click or low-interaction device compromise, exposing personal data and enabling spyware installation.
cards.defend: Install the latest Samsung security maintenance release (SMR) that patches libimagecodec. Encourage users to keep automatic updates enabled and be cautious with unsolicited media from unknown senders.

cards.title: Meteobridge Unauthenticated Command Injection
cards.what: Smartbedded Meteobridge weather-station gateways contain a command injection flaw reachable without authentication. Attackers can execute arbitrary OS commands as root.
cards.why: Root command execution gives full control of the device, allowing it to be used for pivoting, botnet recruitment, or manipulation of monitored data.
cards.defend: Update Meteobridge firmware to the fixed version and never expose the device's web interface directly to the internet. Place it behind a firewall/VPN and monitor for unexpected outbound connections.

cards.title: Internet Explorer Uninitialized Memory Corruption RCE
cards.what: A memory corruption flaw in older versions of Internet Explorer caused by use of uninitialized memory when rendering certain web content. A crafted webpage can trigger the flaw to run arbitrary code.
cards.why: Successful exploitation gives an attacker the same rights as the logged-in user, enabling drive-by compromise simply from visiting a malicious page. The product is end-of-life, so no fixes are forthcoming.
cards.defend: Discontinue use of Internet Explorer and migrate to a supported, patched browser. Remove or restrict legacy browser access and use modern endpoint protection to block malicious sites.

cards.title: Windows Common Log File System Driver Privilege Escalation
cards.what: A privilege escalation flaw in the Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) driver. A local attacker who already has some access can abuse it to bypass security mechanisms and elevate privileges.
cards.why: Attackers commonly chain local privilege escalation with initial access to gain SYSTEM-level control, deepening a foothold and defeating protections. CLFS bugs are a repeat target in real-world intrusions.
cards.defend: Apply the Microsoft security update that addresses this CVE. Limit local access, monitor for suspicious privilege changes, and keep EDR tuned for kernel driver abuse.

cards.title: Windows InformationCardSigninHelper ActiveX Out-of-Bounds Write
cards.what: An out-of-bounds write in the InformationCardSigninHelper ActiveX control (icardie.dll) in Windows. A specially crafted webpage viewed in the browser can trigger the flaw.
cards.why: Exploitation allows remote code execution with the current user's rights, enabling drive-by attacks. The affected product may be end-of-life with no available patch.
cards.defend: Apply vendor updates where available, or set the kill bit to disable the vulnerable ActiveX control. Discontinue use of unsupported products and restrict ActiveX in the browser.

cards.title: Windows TrueType Font Parsing Kernel RCE
cards.what: A vulnerability in the TrueType font parsing engine within win32k.sys kernel-mode driver. Crafted font data embedded in a document or webpage can trigger code execution in the kernel.
cards.why: Because parsing happens in kernel mode, exploitation can grant full system control from merely opening a document or page. This technique was famously used by the Duqu malware.
cards.defend: Apply the relevant Microsoft security update. Restrict embedded fonts, deploy attack surface reduction rules, and use content filtering to block malicious documents.

cards.title: Mozilla Firefox/SeaMonkey/Thunderbird JavaScript Memory Corruption
cards.what: A memory corruption flaw in Firefox, SeaMonkey, and Thunderbird triggered via JavaScript involving frame construction and appendChild index tracking. Malicious content can corrupt memory and run code.
cards.why: With JavaScript enabled, simply viewing a malicious page or message could lead to remote code execution as the user. This was exploited in the wild via drive-by attacks.
cards.defend: Update to a fixed Mozilla release. Keep browsers and mail clients current, and use script controls or reputation-based filtering to reduce exposure to malicious content.

cards.title: Oracle E-Business Suite BI Publisher Unauthenticated Takeover
cards.what: An unspecified vulnerability in the BI Publisher Integration component of Oracle E-Business Suite. An unauthenticated attacker with HTTP network access can compromise Oracle Concurrent Processing.
cards.why: Successful attacks lead to full takeover of Oracle Concurrent Processing without credentials, and the flaw is linked to ransomware activity. Internet-exposed EBS instances are high-value targets.
cards.defend: Apply Oracle's emergency security update immediately. Restrict internet exposure of EBS, place it behind access controls, and monitor for anomalous HTTP requests and processing activity.
